items.title: EC: No proposal to increase Sarawak parliamentary seats
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Election Commission (EC) said there is currently no proposal to increase the number of parliamentary constituencies in Sarawak, contrary to a local newspaper report linking the matter to discussions on the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63). EC secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus said the report cited a purported document on the proposed redelineation of Sarawak's parliamentary constituencies, which the newspaper claimed to have obtained. The local Malay-language newspaper had earlier reported that the proposed redelineation exercise would see the number of parliamentary constituencies in Sarawak increase from 31 to 46, citing a document purportedly outlining the exercise.

items.title: Pas prepares to contest Bersatu-held Kuala Sentul, Lepar
items.summary: KUANTAN: Pas has begun preparations to contest the Kuala Sentul and Lepar state seats, which were won by Perikatan Nasional (PN) in the 15th general election (GE15). Pahang Pas commissioner Datuk Rosli Abdul Jabar said there was no longer an alliance between Pas and Bersatu following the split between the two parties, while the assemblymen for both seats now support the Barisan Nasional (BN) state government. Following GE15, Pahang PN had 17 elected representatives — 15 from Pas and two from Bersatu.

items.title: Ex-army corporal acquitted of 17 charges, including 15 molestation counts
items.summary: Magistrate Uthman Abd Ghani made the decision after finding that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case against the accused, Mohd Amanah Habhijullah, 38. He said the dates and times for each charge had not been specified, leaving the prosecution case heavily reliant on the evidence of the complainant, who was also the first prosecution witness (SP1). Uthman said there were discrepancies between SP1's police report and his testimony in court, particularly concerning the accused's actions after the alleged incident on Oct 14, 2023.

items.title: Anwar wants small traders to suggest aid recipients ahead of 2027 Budget
items.summary: ALOR SETAR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants small entrepreneurs in every village to propose fellow traders who should receive government assistance under the planned increase in allocation for the group in 2027 Budget. Anwar said many stalls run by small entrepreneurs also provided employment, helping to generate income for the local community. Meanwhile, Anwar said the government would continue attracting major foreign investments to boost the country's economy while ensuring the entry of foreign companies did not affect local enterprises, particularly small entrepreneurs.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - September 25, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Najib cannot pay Datuk Seri Najib Razak's lawyer says he cannot afford the RM50 million fine imposed under his house arrest conditions. Ismail urged to explain Former Negri Sembilan menteri besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun has urged Datuk Ismail Lasim to explain why he signed the proclamation. Anwar buries brother Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's elder brother Idrus Ibrahim was laid to rest after Friday prayers, with hundreds attending the funeral.

items.title: Malaysia calls for greater burden-sharing over Rohingya crisis
items.summary: NEW YORK: Malaysia has called for greater burden-sharing and international responsibility to support countries hosting Rohingya refugees amid the prolonged crisis in Myanmar. "Malaysia remains deeply concerned about the prolonged conflict and worsening humanitarian situation in Myanmar, particularly the continued suffering of the Rohingya, which has also had a significant impact on Malaysia," he said. In support of the legal efforts, Malaysia was also actively contributing to the OIC Fund for Rohingya, Mohamad said.

items.title: Between China Glut and increasingly irrational West, Malaysian automotive market is stuck between a rock and a hard place
items.summary: SCROLL through any local EV forum or social media comment section today, and you will find a consistent chorus of anger. When the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry tightened its regulatory stance with protective walls - such as the minimum RM200,000 CIF threshold and 180 kW motor output floors for fully imported (CBU) electric vehicles - the digital reaction was swift and predictable. Then last week, Thailand - which had previously been very bullish on electric vehicles - decided to slam the brakes on imports as well, instituting higher tariffs and even stricter local content requirements for vehicles assembled within their borders.

items.title: Yinson privatisation talks continue, indicative price unchanged
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Yinson Holdings Bhd and MISC Bhd say talks on a potential privatisation of Yinson are ongoing, with the indicative offer price maintained at RM2.35 a share. The letter confirmed that Yinson Legacy was in talks with MISC and the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) to take Yinson private. Following completion, MISC and Yinson Legacy are expected to hold equal stakes in Yinson.

items.title: Bandar Utama school stabbing: Victim's family to file civil suit
items.summary: The victim's mother, Wong Lee Ping, said the family had officially appointed lawyers to initiate civil proceedings against relevant parties to seek accountability, particularly over possible negligence in preventing the incident. Meanwhile, Lim said lawyers at his service centre would provide full legal support to the victim's family. "On Sept 22, the A-GC officially filed a notice of appeal at the Court of Appeal against the High Court's decision.

items.title: Kuching Marathon cancellation a blow to 13,000 participants who made travel plans, says Sarawak sports minister
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 25 — Sarawak Youth, Sports and Entrepreneur Development Minister Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah has expressed disappointment over the last-minute cancellation of Kuching Marathon 2026, which had attracted more than 13,000 registered participants. He said the decision was particularly difficult for participants from outside Sarawak who had made advance arrangements, including booking flights and accommodation. Meanwhile, KMA said registered participants could collect their finisher medals and finisher tees tomorrow (Sept 26) and Sunday at the Alfresco area of Plaza Merdeka Shopping Centre.

items.title: Talk of US export ban on diesel deepens US crude futures' discount to global benchmark
items.summary: HOUSTON: Washington's talk of a possible ban on diesel exports is widening the gap between US crude oil futures and the global Brent benchmark, a signal that markets expect US refiners to process less crude oil if their diesel output gets stuck at home. As investors price in a scenario where diesel gets stranded in the US, West Texas Intermediate crude futures traded as much as US$12.02 a barrel under Brent futures on Thursday, their largest discount since May 6, according to LSEG data. The prospects for a US diesel export ban remain uncertain.

items.title: Negri Sembilan government portal removes photos of 10 exco members
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Photos of 10 Negri Sembilan executive councillors (exco) have reportedly been removed from the official state government portal. The gazette, dated Sept 24, stated that the appointments of the 10 exco members were revoked with effect from Sept 20 by Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir under Article 38(5) of the Constitution of the State of Negri Sembilan 1959. The exco members are Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli, Datuk Zaifulbahri Idris, Datuk Mustapha Nagoor, Siow Kong Choon, Siti Nur Umaira Hasim, Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Suhaimizan Bizar, Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa and Datuk Razali Abu Samah.

items.title: Insas seeks shareholders' nod for RM530mil Inari exit
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Insas Bhd, the third-largest shareholder in Inari Amertron Bhd, is seeking shareholders' approval to dispose of its entire stake in the semiconductor services company for RM529.87 million. As at Aug 31, 2026, Insas had total borrowings of RM449 million. Insas originally invested about RM23.72 million in the shares.

items.title: EC: 43,309 new voters added in August — check the electoral roll by October 24
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 25 — The Supplementary Electoral Roll for August 2026 (DPT BLN8/2026) is open for review for 30 days until Oct 24, said Election Commission (EC) secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus. Khairul Shahril said it also includes 34,411registered voters who have changed their electoral constituencies and 2,728 voters who have changed their voter category or status. “Checks can be made via the EC portal at https://www.spr.gov.my or https://mysprsemak.spr.gov.my, the official state election office portal at http://ppn.spr.gov.my, the online application at https://myspr.spr.gov.my, the MySPR Semak mobile application, or the Voter Registration Check hotline at 03-8892 7218,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: ETA trims stake in Indonesian canned food unit Rex Canning
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: ETA Group Bhd, formerly Rex Industry Bhd, is disposing of its 38 per cent stake in Indonesian canned food maker PT Rex Canning and its entire interest in dormant subsidiary Rex Foods Sdn Bhd for RM22.73 million cash. In a bourse filing, the company said it entered into a share sale agreement with VIP Bonanza Sdn Bhd, with RM14.04 million attributable to its 38 per cent stake in Rex Canning and RM8.68 million for its 100 per cent stake in Rex Foods. Upon completion, ETA will retain a 62 per cent stake in Rex Canning, which will remain its subsidiary.

items.title: Favelle Favco secures RM88.8mil crane orders
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Favelle Favco Bhd's unit Favelle Favco Cranes (M) Sdn Bhd has bagged three offshore crane orders worth a combined RM88.8 million. The orders comprise the supply of offshore cranes to Saipem Offshore Construction SPA, Malaysia Marine and Heavy Engineering Sdn Bhd and OceanMight Sdn Bhd. Favelle Favco said the crane for Saipem Offshore Construction and the one for Malaysia Marine and Heavy Engineering are expected to be delivered by the end of 2027.

items.title: Dollar falls as oil cools but set for weekly gain, yen rallies
items.summary: HONG KONG/LONDON: The dollar fell on Friday but was on track for its second consecutive weekly gain on rising rate hike bets, while the yen rallied after Japan said Tokyo and Washington remain committed to the stance behind July's joint intervention. Sterling rose 0.3 per cent to US$1.326, boosted by hawkish comments from Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey. Markets have aggressively repriced the US interest rate trajectory after the Federal Reserve tightened policy last week.

items.title: 'A significant legacy in arts and culture': Anwar pays tribute to L. Krishnan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim paid tribute to veteran film director Tan Sri Lakshmanan Krishnan, better known as L. Krishnan, who died at 104, describing him as one of the early figures who helped shape Malay cinema. "The late L. Krishnan was a former student of Bukit Mertajam High School and among the earliest figures to shape the development of Malay cinema," he said in a social media post today. Anwar said L. Krishnan produced important works during the 1950s and 1960s with prominent production houses, including Shaw Brothers, Malay Film Productions, Cathay-Keris and Merdeka Studios.

items.title: [UPDATED] Malaysian Bar to challenge Najib's house arrest pardon
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Bar will challenge the Federal Territories Pardons Board's decision and advice concerning Datuk Seri Najib Razak's second pardon, which allows him to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest. Its president Anand Raj said the Bar, through its solicitors, would challenge the decision and advice concerning the second pardon while maintaining its appeal against the board's 2024 decision to reduce Najib's prison sentence and fine. "The Malaysian Bar will, through its solicitors, challenge the decision and advice of the Pardons Board concerning the Second Pardon, while maintaining its appeal in relation to the Pardons Board's decision and advice on the First Pardon," he said in a statement today.

items.title: Nancy urges women to be bold, lead with clear vision
items.summary: KUCHING: Women need the courage to step forward to lead and set a clear direction to play a greater role in shaping society, said Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri. She said leadership is not merely about politics or holding key positions, but about helping communities and meeting others' needs. "Leaders must also possess high empathy and align their leadership spirit with actions to benefit the community," she said at the opening of the Apprentice Programme: Dayak Women and Grassroots Leadership in Governance, Decision-Making and Sustainable Development here today.

items.title: Anwar hails Malaysia’s Asian Games sepak takraw gold after 36-year wait
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated the national men’s sepak takraw squad on winning the team regu gold medal at the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games today. Syabas (Well done) Malaysia. Earlier, the national sepak takraw squad clinched the men’s team regu gold medal after defeating Thailand 2-0 in the final at the Paloma Mizuho Arena.

items.title: Three Sarawak areas record unhealthy API readings at 6pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Three areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 6pm today, down from four at 2pm after Sri Aman improved to the moderate category. Serian recorded the highest reading at 169, down from 174 at 2pm. Sri Aman recorded 98, the highest reading in the moderate category, after registering 156 at 2pm.

items.title: Immigration detains 84 foreign nationals in two-phase raid at Putrajaya’s ‘Green Flats’
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 25 — The Immigration Department detained 84 foreign nationals under Ops Pintu at Pangsapuri Putra Harmoni, better known as the “Green Flats”, here following intelligence gathering and public tip-offs. It said 60 Immigration personnel conducted the operation in two phases beginning yesterday. It said 321 people were inspected, while 84 foreign nationals — 73 men, nine women and two children — were detained for further investigation.

items.title: Zahid applauds national heroes after historic sepak takraw gold
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has congratulated the national men's sepak takraw squad on winning the team regu gold medal at the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games today. "Alhamdulillah, after a 36-year wait, the gold medal finally belongs to Malaysia once again. My congratulations to the national men's sepak takraw squad for their proud achievement in the team regu event at the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games today.

items.title: Malaysia among 'fabulous five' Asean economies set to attract more FDI – Economist
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is among five Asean economies poised to attract more foreign direct investment (FDI), supported by their strengths in manufacturing and digital infrastructure. Juwai IQI global chief economist Shan Saeed said the five economies — Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, the Philippines and Vietnam — are well placed to benefit as investment shifts towards productive capacity in the region. He also estimated that the five economies accounted for US$84.8 billion, or about 80 per cent, of Asean's US$105.6 billion in announced greenfield investment.

items.title: Anwar congratulates sepak takraw squad
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim congratulated the national men's sepak takraw team after they ended a 36-year wait for the Asian Games team regu gold medal in Aichi-Nagoya today. "Congratulations to the national sepak takraw squad on ending a 36-year wait to win gold again in the men's team regu event at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026," he said in a social media post. The victory was particularly significant for the sepak takraw team, who last won the team regu gold at the 1990 Beijing Asian Games, when they also defeated Thailand in the final.

items.title: Orang Asli woman missing after fishing trip in Rompin
items.summary: ROMPIN: An Orang Asli woman has been reported missing after she failed to return home from a fishing trip near Kampung Lesung, Kedaik, here on Sept 22. Kuang Poh, 73, from Kampung Api Larat in Pekan, was last seen leaving her home for the swampy area near Kampung Lesung about 3pm. Rompin district police chief Superintendent Sharif Shai Sharif Mondoi said a relative lodged a police report at about 5pm on Sept 23 after being alerted by a family member.

items.title: Singapore population hits 6.21 million as non-resident numbers climb
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Singapore's total population rose 1.6 per cent year-on-year to 6.21 million as of June 2026, from 6.11 million a year earlier, according to the National Population and Talent Division (NPTD). In its Population In Brief 2026 report released on Friday, NPTD said the citizen population increased by 0.7 per cent to 3.68 million in June 2026 from 3.66 million in the previous year, while the permanent resident population remained relatively stable at 0.55 million. "The non-resident population stood at 1.98 million in June 2026, an increase of 3.7 per cent from June 2025," it said.

items.title: SkyWorld on track for RM4.6bil GDV target
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: SkyWorld Development Bhd says it is on track to achieve RM4.6 billion in cumulative post-listing gross development value (GDV) launches by the end of 2026. This will be supported by new launches targeted for the year, totalling more than RM2.0 billion. Chief executive officer Lee Chee Seng said the property developer has RM1.1 billion in unbilled sales, which provides earnings visibility as it works to strengthen its financial performance.

items.title: China leaves business leaders at home as Xi courts Trump in Washington
items.summary: BEIJING: Chinese business executives were notably absent during President Xi Jinping's visit to Washington, a stark contrast to the titans of US business turning out for a black-tie dinner at the White House. Apart from Xi and his wife Peng Liyuan, the Chinese delegation included his right-hand man Cai Qi, the country's top diplomat Wang Yi and Chinese ambassador to the United States and top trade negotiator He Lifeng. The Chinese foreign ministry refused to comment when asked by reporters whether a trade delegation would travel with Xi.

items.title: Two tahfiz students charged with injuring schoolmate with iron
items.summary: PARIT: Two tahfiz school students, aged 13 and 14, were charged in the magistrate's court here today with injuring a fellow student with an iron. They pleaded not guilty after the charge was read before magistrate Nurul Izalina Rajaai in closed-door proceedings. Deputy public prosecutor R. Jayasri prosecuted, while the two students were represented by National Legal Aid Foundation lawyer Nur Nadrah Badarudin.

items.title: Malaysian Bar seeks disclosure of taxpayer cost of Najib house arrest, plans fresh court challenge
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — The Malaysian government should disclose the additional cost to taxpayers if former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak serves the remainder of his SRC International jail term under house arrest, Malaysian Bar president Anand Raj said today. In a statement, Anand urged the Federal Territories Pardons Board and the Prime Minister’s Department to disclose two things to the public: “Declassify and publish the official minutes of the Pardons Board meeting(s) held regarding Najib’s First Pardon and Najib’s Second Pardon decisions”; and “Fully disclose all conditions proposed to be attached to Najib’s house arrest, including monitoring protocols, enforcement authorities and the additional costs to taxpayers that a ‘house arrest’ would entail.” Anand also announced today that the Malaysian Bar would go to court to challenge the Pardons Board’s decision and advice concerning Najib’s second pardon.

items.title: Ringgit closes higher against US dollar despite Fed rate hike expectations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit closed higher against the US dollar on Friday, driven by bargain-hunting activity despite expectations of further US interest rate hikes. At 6pm, the ringgit increased to 4.0715/0765 versus the greenback from Thursday's close of 4.0840/0880. He said the US Dollar Index (DXY) remained well supported at 101.182 points as the odds of the Federal Reserve (Fed) raising interest rates stayed high.

items.title: SUV driver held after fatal crash with motorcyclist in Kuantan
items.summary: KUANTAN: Police have detained the driver of a sports utility vehicle (SUV) after his vehicle allegedly crashed into an oncoming motorcyclist, killing the rider near a petrol station along Jalan Semambu here today. Kuantan police chief Assistant Commissioner Ashari Abu Samah said the 56-year-old motorcyclist, who was travelling alone, was killed in the 8am crash. Ashari said the motorcyclist suffered severe injuries and died at the scene.

items.title: Johari: Corruption risks must be spotted early, not addressed later
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Integrity units in every organisation must to be empowered as strategic partners to top management in identifying corruption risks at an early stage, rather than merely handling complaints or follow-up action after violations occur. Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul said the units should also play a role in addressing systemic weaknesses and fostering a culture of integrity within organisations. He said corruption prevention must begin before a case occurs through good governance, effective control systems, education, workplace culture and values instilled in every individual.

items.title: EC denies report of 15 new parliamentary seats for Sarawak
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 25 — The Election Commission (EC) has denied a report claiming that Sarawak’s parliamentary constituencies would be increased, saying there is currently no proposal to alter the number of federal seats in the state. EC secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus said no documents had been shared indicating that Sarawak’s parliamentary constituencies would be increased to any particular number. The review proposes 17 new state constituencies, increasing the number of Sarawak Legislative Assembly seats from 82 to 99, as well as changes to the names of several existing state constituencies and one parliamentary constituency.

items.title: MACC completes Kedah fertiliser probe, two may face charges soon
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 25 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has completed its investigation into the delayed supply of fertilisers in Kedah, with two individuals set to be charged soon in connection with the case. “The MACC investigation into the issue of fertiliser distribution to farmers and paddy planters in Kedah has been completed. On September 7, the MACC opened an investigation paper into the delayed distribution of Additional Compound Fertiliser, or Paddy Fertiliser 3, to Kedah paddy farmers.

items.title: MACC chief: Two former Felda officials to be charged over Kuala Lumpur Vertical City project next week
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 25 — Two individuals being investigated over alleged misappropriation involving the Kuala Lumpur Vertical City (KLVC) project linked to Felda will be charged next week, Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said. He said the two were a former Felda general manager and a former chief executive officer of Felda Investment Committee, also known as Felda Investment Commission. The KLVC investigation is among seven investigation papers involving Felda and Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC), comprising six new investigation papers and one previous investigation.

items.title: More questioning awaits Isa Samad in Felda probe once he recovers from eye surgery, says MACC
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 25 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) will resume recording the statement of Datuk Seri Isa Samad once the former Felda chairman recovers from a medical procedure. MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said Isa is being treated at the Serdang Hospital after undergoing eye surgery. “Regarding Isa’s statement, we had to put it on hold.

items.title: Witness tails fleeing hatchback after attempted theft, helping police make arrest in Sarawak
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 25 — A witness who followed a hatchback believed to have been used by two men fleeing an attempted vehicle component theft helped police trace their movements and arrest one suspect here last night. He said the witness spotted two men allegedly attempting to steal components from a vehicle parked outside the workshop. “A witness noticed two suspicious men trying to steal the components from a vehicle parked outside the workshop before they fled using the hatchback after being confronted.

items.title: MACC to issue asset declaration notices to Saravanan, his wife and three children
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 25 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) will issue notices to former human resources minister Datuk Seri M Saravanan, his wife, and their three children to declare their assets within a month. Its chief commissioner, Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman, said that the asset declaration notice under Section 36 of the MACC Act 2009 will be delivered on Monday to Saravanan, his wife, and their two children, while another child who is still abroad will receive it in November. In another development, Abd Halim said his side has not yet received the asset declaration from the former chairman of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim, and his family.

items.title: Perak court fines buyer, petrol station owner RM25,000 each over RON95 sale to Singapore car
items.summary: MANJUNG, Sept 25 — An oil palm plantation worker and a petrol station owner were each fined RM25,000 by the Sessions Court here today for their involvement in buying and selling RON95 petrol for foreign-registered vehicles. Wong was charged with violating Regulation 4(1) of the Control of Supplies Regulations (Prohibition of Sale and Purchase of Controlled Goods) for purchasing 27.452 litres of RON95 petrol for use in a foreign-registered (Singapore) vehicle. Meanwhile, Ling was charged — at the same date, time, and location — with violating Regulation 3(1) of the Control of Supplies Regulations (Prohibition of Sale and Purchase of Controlled Goods) for selling the same petrol to Wong for use in a foreign-registered (Singapore) vehicle.

items.title: When will Melaka vote? EC to decide key state election dates on October 7
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — The Election Commission (EC) will hold a special meeting on October 7 to discuss matters related to the 16th Melaka state election. EC secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus said the special meeting followed the dissolution of the Melaka State Assembly last Wednesday. “The special meeting will be chaired by EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun.

items.title: Haze forces Kuching Marathon 2026 cancellation at eleventh hour
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 25 — The Kuching Marathon 2026 scheduled for Sunday (September 27) has been cancelled due to the prevailing haze situation affecting Kuching and surrounding areas. In announcing the cancellation, the Kuching Marathon Association (KMA) said it had been continuously monitoring Air Pollutant Index (API) readings and other environmental indicators since the onset of the haze. He also said more than 13,000 participants had registered for this year’s Kuching Marathon.

items.title: PM’s brother Idrus Ibrahim buried in Bukit Mertajam after Friday prayers
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM, Sept 25 — The remains of Idrus Ibrahim, the elder brother of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, were laid to rest at the Cheruk Tok Kun Bawah Muslim Cemetery here today. The funeral was attended by hundreds of family members, relatives, friends and political leaders from various parties. The prime minister, accompanied by family members and members of the public, walked about 200 metres from the late Idrus’ home to the prayer hall.

items.title: Woman dies after Honda Jazz loses control, crashes into lorry in Kulai
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — A 32-year-old woman with a hearing disability died after the Honda Jazz she was driving crashed into the rear of a lorry at KM32 of Jalan Johor Bahru-Air Hitam here early today. The woman, who worked as a general worker at a technology park in Kulai, suffered severe head injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene, while the 66-year-old local lorry driver sustained minor injuries, Utusan Malaysia reported. Kulai district police chief Assistant Commissioner Tan Seng Lee said police received information about the crash at about 6.15am.

items.title: Vulnerable groups to be focus of Selangor Budget 2027, says MB
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Supporting vulnerable groups will be among the Selangor government’s main priorities in Budget 2027, with the aim of ensuring the state’s economic progress benefits people across all segments of society. Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said Selangor’s development should go beyond strong economic performance and attracting investment to also addressing the needs of groups requiring greater attention, according to a Berita Harian report published today. Amirudin said existing support programmes, including cash handouts and assistance under Bantuan Kehidupan Sejahtera Selangor (Bingkas) and YANIS, would be part of efforts to help vulnerable groups, including those affected by the current energy supply crisis.

items.title: Appeals court lets MAIWP strike out man’s bid to change religion from Islam to Sikhism
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 25 — The Court of Appeal today allowed appeals by the Federal Territory Islamic Religious Council (MAIWP) and the government to strike out a man’s suit challenging his religious status. The three-judge panel comprising Justices Datuk Seri Mohd Firuz Jaffril, Datuk Faizah Jamaludin and Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid ruled that Shehzad Malik Muhammad Sarwar Malik’s case was a renunciation case and the relief he is seeking could only be granted by the Syariah Court. “The respondent (Shehzad Malik) here cannot come to the Civil Court as the Civil Court has no jurisdiction to grant the orders,” said Justice Mohd Firuz, who delivered the unanimous decision.

items.title: Anwar wraps China visit with RM36.8b in trade, investment pledges
items.summary: HANGZHOU, Sept 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's three-day working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou, China, is not just a routine diplomatic trip, but rather a new benchmark for the continuation of strategic relations that strengthen cooperation in various fields between the two countries. The working visit at the invitation of the Chinese government not only strengthens bilateral relations, but also opens up new opportunities for Malaysia to expand investments, export markets and cooperation in strategic and high-value economic areas. Summarising the overall outcome of the visit, Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, said the relationship between Malaysia and China is now at a very strong level and is developing positively.

items.title: In Johor, Indonesian teen charged with trafficking over 25kg of illicit drugs
items.summary: The charge was framed under Section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, punishable under Section 39B(2) of the same Act. The offense was also framed under Section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 and is punishable under Section 39B(2) of the same Act. The charge was brought under Section 12(2) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 for illegal possession of drugs and is punishable under Section 39A(1) of the same Act.

items.title: Spell out the offence: Aminudin challenges Negeri MB over royal dispute allegations
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 25 — Former Negeri Sembilan menteri besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun has called on current Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim to specify the alleged shortcomings of the previous administration that led to issues involving the state’s customary traditions and royal institution. Aminuddin said the public had the right to know what actions were allegedly not taken during his tenure as Menteri Besar, including the specific provisions of the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan (UUTKNS) 1959 that were allegedly breached and when the alleged violation occurred. "What actions were said to have been overlooked?

items.title: Negeri Sembilan Undang, disputed chiefs: Conference of Rulers told of Tunku Nadzaruddin’s succession
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — The Negeri Sembilan government has notified the Conference of Rulers of Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar’s selection as the state’s 12th Yang di-Pertuan Besar, according to an Undang and three ruling chiefs whose positions are disputed. The group said the notification meant Tunku Nadzaruddin was the only person with lawful authority to perform the functions of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar under the Negeri Sembilan Constitution 1959, including attending meetings of the Conference of Rulers, The Star reported today. “The state government administration must also immediately accord all privileges and entitlements prescribed for Tunku Nadzaruddin,” they said.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan undangs tell PM, AGC to stay out of state affairs
items.summary: In a press conference in Seremban today, the group said Articles 10 and 11 of the Negeri Sembilan Constitution 1959 vested the Undang Yang Empat with exclusive authority to appoint and remove the state ruler, Free Malaysia Today reported. They also cautioned Anwar against using federal agencies in ways that could disrupt the administration of Negeri Sembilan. Do not sow disorder in our state using federal government agencies to paralyse the state government.

items.title: Najib may walk out of Kajang Prison next month if High Court stays 15-year 1MDB sentence and RM50m fine is paid, says lawyer
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak could leave Kajang Prison as early as next month to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest if the High Court grants a stay of his 15-year 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) sentence, his lawyer Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah said today. The High Court has fixed October 14 to hear Najib’s application to stay the execution of his 15-year prison sentence in the 1MDB case pending his appeal. Shafee said the defence had sought the stay of the 1MDB sentence following the conditional pardon granted to Najib.

items.title: Malaysia, Indonesia form joint Halal Council to strengthen bilateral trade
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Malaysia announced the establishment of the Malaysia-Indonesia Halal Council in a bid to strengthen halal diplomacy between the two countries, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today. "Next month, the focus is on facilitating halal certification between Malaysia and Indonesia to ease bilateral halal trade between the two countries," he said in his speech at the Global Halal Summit 2026 here today. Ahmad Zahid said the council would build on existing bilateral cooperation between Malaysia and Indonesia to address differing halal requirements, repeated procedures and difficulties faced by businesses seeking to enter neighbouring markets.

items.title: KTMB apologises after absent staff strands 25 riders at Anak Bukit station
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) has apologised to affected passengers following an incident in which the Anak Bukit Station main gate failed to open as scheduled early this morning. KTMB said preliminary investigations found that the station was scheduled to begin operations at 5.30 am, but the staff member assigned to work failed to report for duty due to health reasons. “Immediate action was taken by instructing a counter clerk from a nearby station, who was scheduled to report for duty at 7 am, to arrive earlier at Anak Bukit Station,” KTMB said in a statement.

items.title: ‘Suspicion cannot take the place of proof’: BFM ordered to pay ex-presenter RM358,400 over 2019 dismissal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — The Industrial Court has ordered BFM Media Sdn Bhd to pay former producer and presenter Umapagan Ampikaipakan RM358,400 after ruling that the radio station failed to prove the misconduct allegations used to justify his dismissal in 2019. While the allegations against Umapagan were serious, Industrial Court chairman Pravin Kaur Jessy found that BFM had not proved the alleged misconduct on the balance of probabilities, The Edge Malaysia reported yesterday. BFM had accused Umapagan of sexual harassment and other misconduct, including sending explicit messages, making inappropriate remarks and engaging in unwanted physical contact.

items.title: Immigration busts Indonesians making RM50,000 monthly via illegal beauty treatments
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 25 — The Immigration Department (JIM) detained seven Indonesian nationals believed to be working as beauty therapists in a special operation at four locations in Shah Alam, Pandan Perdana and Kepong last Wednesday. JIM, in a statement today, said those detained comprised one man and six women aged between 19 and 44. JIM said two women and a man were detained under Section 15(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63, while three women were detained under Section 6(1)(c) of the same Act.

items.title: Fadhlina: SMKA Jempol to become first TVET religious school in Malaysia
items.summary: JEMPOL, Sept 25 — Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Agama (SMKA) Jempol will become the country’s first Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) religious-stream school. Insya-Allah, SMKA Jempol will be the first SMKA to adopt or introduce TVET. Meanwhile, she said religious school students in the country were also encouraged to master various languages as an important medium for strengthening the dakwah agenda more effectively.
